title: Boot recovery eagerly rebinds every session that ever bound, spawning about 25 `engram control` sidecars within two minutes of a restart on one store, instead of rebinding lazily on the first turn
outcome: After a restart the host does not rebind every idle session that still carries a routing token, grant or rebind flag (engram_boot_recovery_candidate_locked, engram_host_adapter.rs:3963-3972; targets :3996-4043; coordinator :4116-4247): sessions with nothing queued and no open grant rebind lazily at their first admission, so a restart spawns sidecars only for sessions that need reconciliation now, and the Engram store is not opened by 25 processes at once. Measured 2026-10-22: host PID 130532 up 18:46:00.957Z; 25 `engram control` children spawned 18:46:09-18:47:49Z (13 Engram, 9 TermAl, 2 PhoenixCodeNav, 1 fit_friends; idle sessions among them) plus 4 `engram mcp`, all on C:\Users\grzeg\.engram (1.08 GB); each lives 5 min idle (ENGRAM_CONTROL_IDLE_TIMEOUT, engram_control_transport.rs:12); in the same minutes evaluate took 18-28 s against a 20 s budget.
acceptance: A note states, from code with file:line, which boot-recovery targets need an eager rebind at boot (an open or uncertain grant, a retained queued intent, an unsettled finished child) and which can be left to lazy rebind at first admission (idle sessions with only a routing token or rebind flag).

Tests over the candidate filter and first-admission path show that only sessions in the eager classes are rebound at boot and the rest rebind lazily on their first admission with no change to correctness (a lazily rebound session's first turn still reconciles its token and grants exactly as boot recovery did).
The full five-stage gate passes on the exact frozen input intended for landing, with an independent review pair and no outstanding in-scope Medium-or-higher finding.
The batch's live and post-restart criteria are preserved verbatim in linked item w-7a9b4163c18a, "v3 admission recovery: post-restart live verification"; this item's evidence links to that item.
